title: Niger–Congo languages - Wikipedia
text: Niger–Congo is a proposed family of African languages spoken over the majority of sub-Saharan Africa. It unites the Mande languages, the Atlantic–Congo languages, and possibly several smaller groups of languages that are difficult to classify.

title: Benue-Congo languages | African Language Family | Britannica
text: The Benue-Congo branch includes approximately 900 languages, divided into 11 groups. Ten of these groups are primarily spoken within Nigeria. The 11th group, Bantoid, is the largest within the Benue-Congo and Niger-Congo families.

title: Benue-Congo Languages | Language and... | EBSCO Research
text: The Benue-Congo languages are divided into eleven groups: Oko, Ukaan-Akpes, Defoid, Edoid, Nupoid, Idomoid, Igboid, Kainji, Platoid, Cross River, and Bantoid. Ten of these groups are almost exclusive to Nigeria.
